messages:
lina-support: FYI inbound from AcmeCorp — multiple 5xx/timeouts from hosted inference. customer sees p95/p99 spikes and many `504` on chat endpoint. correlation id: cid=acme-8311-01
ryan-oncall: Investigating. Any PSA on broad impact or single tenant?
mike-sre: Metrics look like gateway queue depth for hosted-route `chat-v1` hit limit at 18:41 UTC. sudden enqueue rate + long continuous-batcher backlog. stack traces show dequeue timeouts.
lina-support: Customer says it started ~18:35 after a small campaign. They included a failing curl: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'` returned 504 and `x-request-id: acme-8311-42`.
mike-sre: Looking at logs for `acme-8311-42` -> gateway returned 504 after 30s deadline, batcher logs: `dequeue_wait > 25000ms`, per-req queue hit soft-limit. Continuous batching backlog jumped 3x.
ops-bot: IncidentBot: PagerDuty incident PDI-899 created and oncall @ryan-oncall notified.
anya-eng: Can we repro with a synthetic at similar qps? I'll spin a small load from staging pointing to hosted-route test tenant.
ryan-oncall: Do we have immediate mitigations? Can we temporarily loosen queue depth or enable early-reject for oversized requests?
mike-sre: Quick wins: 1) disable continuous-batcher on that gateway pool (drops batching but frees dequeue headroom), 2) increase per-route queue depth from 64->96 for 10m, 3) enable tenant-level soft-shed for Acme to throttle. Prefer #1 for fastest effect.
lina-support: Customer asked for ETA. I'll tell them 15 min while we triage.
mike-sre: Applying mitigation: disabling continuous-batcher flag for pool 'hosted-gw-prod-eu-1' (rolling). starting now.
anya-eng: I can run repro after flag flip. running 50 rps synthetic with mix of short+long sequences.
mike-sre: Flag rolled at 18:48 UTC. Observability: dequeue latency dropped, queue depth steady. p95 for gateway fell from 1.8s -> 420ms; tail 99.9 improved.
ryan-oncall: Customer-facing note: send preliminary update that we've applied mitigation and are monitoring. Lina, can you post?
lina-support: Posted to Acme: "We've applied a temporary routing change to reduce batching pressure and are monitoring. If you still see 5xx please share a recent x-request-id." :thumbsup:
mike-sre: Root cause hypothesis: burst from campaign created many long-running requests that inflated continuous-batching KV cache spikes, causing some dequeue slots to stall and queue depth to saturate. Batchers kept waiting for prefix coalescing -> backlog.
anya-eng: Added traces show many requests with long context length (~8k tokens) which immediately occupy batchers longer. That plus default batching window caused tail to pile up.
mike-sre: Next steps: (A) short-term: continue with batching disabled for affected pool until we implement dynamic-batcher-adaptive-window. (B) medium: implement early-reject policy per-tenant when queue depth > 0.8*limit. (C) long: add sequence-length-aware routing to push long requests to separate pool.
ryan-oncall: Create tickets for (B) and (C) and schedule postmortem.
ops-bot: IncidentBot: Runbook link https://redwood.internal/runbooks/queue-saturation — recommended checks performed: queue_depth, dequeue_latency, continuous_batcher_backlog.
lina-support: Customer acknowledged update and dropped more logs. They see errors decreasing.
mike-sre: Confirming 30m after mitigation: p99 gateway errors for Acme down from 7% -> 0.2%. No other tenants impacted.
anya-eng: Patch queued: PR#4521 to add tenant soft-shedding + metrics alert. Target deploy to canary tomorrow.
ryan-oncall: Closing loop: escalate to EngInfra to look at batcher kernel selection under long sequences. Add monitoring alert for continuous-batcher backlog delta > 50 in 5m.
lina-support: I'll mark customer issue as monitored and will keep them posted. Thanks team.
mike-sre: Filing postmortem stub. will include timeline and the mitigation steps.
lina-support: Closing note: Incident resolved for Acme at 19:05 UTC; followups scheduled.
incident-bot: Incident closed PDI-899 (status: mitigated)
